newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian industrials set for profit upturn.
newsitem.headline: Australian industrials set for profit upturn.

text.p: Australian companies look set for an upturn in profits this financial year, judging by the solid first-half results from industrial companies in recent weeks, analysts say.

Earnings from resource companies like the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd had lagged so far in the reporting season for the first half of the year to June 30, 1997, but the outlook for both the industrial and resource sectors looked encouraging, the analysts said on Friday.
The results so far have produced many surprises on the positive side, almost shutting the door on 18 months of disappointing results, analysts said.
Small industrial companies and banks were among the pick of the earnings crop, they said.
"We think there is a nice turn up in profits this year," said David Rickards, strategist at broker Macquarie Equities.
"Housing has picked up and manufacturing is doing better, so we are pretty positive about the earnings scene for the rest of the year," Rickards told Reuters.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia, pastoral and energy group Wesfarmers Ltd and retailer Woolworths Ltd all reported better-than-expected profits, which the market welcomed by pushing up their share prices.

The smaller companies, corporations not in Australia's top 100 listed companies, which have produced good results include bathroom products and outdoor furniture group GWA International Ltd and contract miner and engineering firm Henry Walker Ltd.
The profits for the six months ended December 31, 1996 have been achieved despite a weak patch in the Australian economy for most of the second half of calendar 1996.
The economy did, however, pick up in the final months of 1996.
This rebound, combined with the three interest rate cuts between July and December last year, have set the tone for a better second half for industrial earnings, analysts said.

A fall in the Australian dollar and firmer metal prices are likely to boost second-half earnings for resource stocks, they said. The local dollar has fallen about five U.S. cents since its six-year peak of US$0.8215 in December 1996.
Base metals giants WMC Ltd and MIM Holdings Ltd, aluminium group Capral Aluminium Ltd and gold miner Placer Pacific Ltd have dug up the most disappointing results among mining companies.

"The last half has been quite disastrous for most commodity companies - they have had the double whammy of falling commodity prices and also the stronger dollar that prevailed in the second half of last year," said Greg Chapman, portfolio manager at County NatWest Australia.
"The dollar has come back quite significantly over the course of the last two or three months which would add to the bottom line of most commodity companies," Chapman said.
"On top of that we are expecting to see improved commodity prices going through 1997," he said.

Merrill Lynch equity strategist John Banos said so far of the 61 companies that have reported their results, which are covered by Merrill Lynch analysts, 39 had been in line with forecasts, nine were on the upside and 13 were disappointments.
"At this stage the earnings season appears to be in line. We are showing modest earnings growth," Banos told Reuters.
"There is a reasonable chance we will see earnings growth in the second half of this calendar year and much stronger earnings growth in calendar 1998," Banos said.
